I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so I would keep to the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits our climate, our water conditions, and the way I know how to manage risk. At my age, I would not chase complicated or high-labor crops. I would rather plant the grain crops I understand well, use improved seed, control fertilizer costs, and aim for steady yield. I would prepare the wheat land with rotary tillage after the summer crop, sow on time in autumn, give enough nitrogen for strong tillering and grain filling, and irrigate at the key stages instead of watering too often. After wheat harvest, I would quickly plant summer maize to catch the season, use hybrid seed for better yield, and focus on one basal fertilizer application plus topdressing, with fewer irrigations if summer rain is decent. For pests and disease, I would spray only when needed but I would not skip basic control, because one bad outbreak can cut yield fast. This way, I keep the work manageable, the costs under control, and the land producing through the full year.
